payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_scheduler.py::test_a_stack_order_refuses_a_parent_it_cannot_stack_on_and_names_the_remedy stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'A parent whose pull request exists is said to have no pushed pull request.' applied to saffron/scheduler.py as an edit. The claim was "Under `stack=True`, a spec whose parent cannot be a stack base is refused. Its reason says the parent is outside the stack order, names the cause, and ends with that cause's remedy. With no task, no pushed sha or no branch, the remedy is to run it to a pull request first. With no pull request URL it is `saffron adopt <id> <pr>`. With no waiting task it is to merge it, or rerun it. The witness drives seven parents. One has no task. One has a waiting task with no push. One has a pushed task at `REJECTED`, and one at `EXHAUSTED`. One has a waiting, pushed task with no branch, and one has no pull request URL. The last has a newest waiting task with no push above an older one that qualified.", and only that witness ran under the edit.
